# The bibliographic corpora {#sec-corpora} @sec-plant-literature draws on two screened corpora. This appendix describes them so the claims there can be checked, extended, or disagreed with. ## What they are @tbl-corpora-files lists the two corpora. ::: {#tbl-corpora-files .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='The two screened corpora: number of records, publication years and subject of each file.'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Corpus | Records|Years |Focus | |:-------------------------|-------:|:---------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |`bibliography_animal.csv` | 324|2018-2026 |optimal contribution, coancestry matrix choice, effective size, allelic richness | |`bibliography_plant.csv` | 687|2017-2026 |diversity quantification, heterotic structure, genetic resources, optimisation | ::: ::: Both are annotated screens, not exhaustive searches. The plant corpus came from 2004 records across 29 plant-breeding queries on Crossref and Europe PMC, of which 687 were retained (relevance 2, related background, or 3, directly relevant; 158 are 3). ## Structure The plant file has the columns `doi`, `year`, `authors`, `title`, `journal`, `citations`, `relevance`, `crop`, `metric_used`, `selection_method`, `contribution`, `url`. The ones that carry the screening annotation are described in @tbl-corpora-columns. ::: {#tbl-corpora-columns .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Annotation columns of the corpus files and what each holds.'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Column |Meaning | |:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------| |`relevance` |3 = directly relevant, 2 = related background | |`crop` |plant corpus only | |`metric_used` / `metric_advocated` |the diversity metrics the record reports | |`selection_method` |plant corpus only | |`theme` |animal corpus only; multi-valued, semicolon-separated | |`contribution` / `relevance_note` |a one-line note on what the record adds | ::: ::: ## Relevance and coverage ::: {#tbl-corpora-relevance .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Number of screened records by relevance score (3 = directly relevant, 2 = related background) in each file.'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Corpus | Relevance 2| Relevance 3| |:------|-----------:|-----------:| |plant | 529| 158| |animal | 235| 89| ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-corpora-crops .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Crop coverage of the directly relevant plant records (relevance 3): the ten most frequent crop labels and their number of records.'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |crop | records| |:-------------------|-------:| |maize | 54| |wheat | 11| |multi-crop | 10| |rice | 9| |none | 7| |sorghum | 5| |barley | 4| |none (general crop) | 4| |potato | 3| |soybean | 3| ::: ::: Maize dominates (@tbl-corpora-crops, @fig-plant-landscape), which is the intended bias -- but it also means every claim in @sec-plant-literature about crops other than maize rests on a handful of records. The publication years of both files are in @fig-corpora-years. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Number of screened records per publication year in the plant file (left, `bibliography_plant.csv`) and the animal file (right, `bibliography_animal.csv`); each bar is a count of records, with no uncertainty, and the two panels do not share a vertical scale. The plant file starts in 2017 with 1 record and is mainly from 2018 onward; the animal file starts in 2018.](93-corpora_files/figure-html/fig-corpora-years-1.png){#fig-corpora-years fig-align='center' fig-alt='Two bar charts of the number of screened records per publication year, plant file on the left and animal file on the right. Both rise from a handful of records or fewer in the earliest year to the largest counts in 2025 and 2026.' width=1050} ::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Left: the usage table `plant_metric_usage.csv` as shipped, records per metric category, maize and other crops; it is an external classification with no producer in this repository and is not recomputed (see @tbl-plant-usage-check in @sec-plant-literature). Right: the ten most frequent crop labels among the screened records, with all labels containing 'maize' pooled; the labels 'none' and empty are left out. In both panels the denominator is the screened records of `bibliography_plant.csv` (relevance 2 or 3), 2017-2026. Red outline: the categories to which @sec-plant-literature maps the recommended metrics (expected heterozygosity for the quantity inside the proportional loss, coancestry, allelic richness, effective size), an approximate and non-unique mapping. Left: records per diversity metric category in the plant usage table, from population structure (303 records) down to effective size or status number (17); each bar is split into maize (dark grey) and other crops (light grey), and red outlines mark expected heterozygosity, marker coancestry, allelic richness and effective size. Right: the ten most frequent crop labels among the screened plant records, maize (197) far ahead of wheat (42), multi-crop (39) and rice (33).' width=1350} ::: ::: ## Themes in the animal corpus The `theme` column is multi-valued. Splitting it: ::: {#tbl-corpora-themes .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Themes of the directly relevant records (relevance 3) of `bibliography_animal.csv`, after splitting the semicolon-separated `theme` field; a record with several themes is counted once in each.'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |theme | records| |:---------------------------------------|-------:| |OCS / contribution optimisation | 68| |Coancestry / relationship matrix choice | 61| |Optimisation algorithms / cost | 27| |Allelic richness / rare alleles | 20| |Effective size | 18| |Heterozygosity / gene diversity | 15| |Core collection / subset selection | 9| ::: ::: ## Querying them The corpora are ordinary CSVs. The queries below count what the shipped `metric_used` column holds; they do not reproduce the usage table of @sec-plant-literature, which is an external classification with no producer here and gives larger counts (@tbl-plant-usage-check compares the two). ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # records that report a coancestry or kinship metric sum(grepl("coancestry|kinship|relatedness", pl$metric_used, ignore.case = TRUE)) #> [1] 12 # records using ROH, and how many of those are maize roh <- grepl("\\bROH\\b|runs of homozygosity", pl$metric_used, ignore.case = TRUE) c(roh_total = sum(roh), roh_maize = sum(roh & grepl("maize", pl$crop, ignore.case = TRUE))) #> roh_total roh_maize #> 0 0 # the most-cited directly relevant maize records mz <- pl[pl$relevance == 3 & grepl("maize", pl$crop, ignore.case = TRUE), ] head(mz[order(-mz$citations), c("year", "title", "citations")], 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # the animal-side records on matrix choice mc <- ani[grepl("Coancestry / relationship matrix choice", ani$theme), ] head(mc[order(-mc$citations), c("year", "title", "citations")], 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| | year|title | citations| |:--|----:|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------:| |1 | 2018|Optimal cross selection for long-term genetic gain in two-part programs with rapid recurrent genomic selection | 156| |90 | 2019|The impact of genomic selection on genetic diversity and genetic gain in three French dairy cattle breeds | 100| |2 | 2020|Management of Genetic Diversity in the Era of Genomics. | 72| |92 | 2019|Genomic Tools for Effective Conservation of Livestock Breed Diversity | 71| |94 | 2020|Molecular genetic analysis of spring wheat core collection using genetic diversity, population structure, and linkage disequilibrium | 65| |3 | 2019|Improving Short- and Long-Term Genetic Gain by Accounting for Within-Family Variance in Optimal Cross-Selection. | 59|
::: ::: ## Limitations **These are abstract screens.** Relevance and the metric annotations were scored from titles and abstracts, not from full texts. A paper that computes a metric without naming it in the abstract is invisible to this table -- which almost certainly understates how often coancestry is computed as an intermediate step. **The queries shaped the answer.** 29 plant-breeding queries were run; a different query set would return a different landscape. The strong maize skew is by design, and the counts for other crops are too small to support a claim about those crops. **"Not established in the retrieved set" means exactly that.** Every such statement in @sec-plant-literature is a claim about *this corpus*, not about the literature as a whole. It is a prompt to look further before assuming novelty, not a proof of it. **Citation counts are a snapshot** at screening time and are already stale. ## Classical references The plant file starts in 2017 (one record; mainly 2018 onward) and the animal file in 2018, so the corpora leave out classical work by construction. The classical results the book rests on are cited from the source literature, and collected in `book/references.bib` with two exceptions stated after the table: @tbl-corpora-classical lists them. ::: {#tbl-corpora-classical .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Classical results the book rests on and the source each is cited from.'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Result |Source | |:-----------------------------------|:------------------------------| |group coancestry |Cockerham (1967) | |molecular / IBS coancestry |Nejati-Javaremi et al. (1997) | |gene diversity, Gst |Nei (1973) | |the subdivided-population partition |Caballero & Toro (2000, 2002) | |status number |Lindgren & Mullin (1997, 1998) | |optimal contribution selection |Meuwissen (1997) | |genomic relationship matrix |VanRaden (2008) | |modified Rogers distance |Wright (1978) | |usefulness criterion |Schnell & Utz (1975) | |differential evolution |Storn & Price (1997) | ::: ::: Wright (1978) and Schnell & Utz (1975) are not in `book/references.bib` and are given in the table by author and year only. A Crossref bibliographic query for each returned no record of either work (for Wright, only reviews of the book), so neither entry was checked against a source record here. ## Reproduce this chapter {.unnumbered} All the code of this chapter, in order and with the explanation kept as comments, is one script: [**93-corpora.R**](https://ederdbs.github.io/QG/downloads/93-corpora.R){download="93-corpora.R"}. Download it, install `hybdiv`, and run it top to bottom in an empty directory; cached results are fetched on first use.
